entry.title: Weather-related closures, impacts across South Florida and the Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: Weather-related closures, impacts across South Florida and the Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: 19: Heavy rain and flooding have prompted school, facility, park and event closures across parts of South Florida. Some closures are limited to today, while others remain in effect until conditions improve. Check with the agency before heading out, since updates may change. Palm Beach County West Palm Beach: The city canceled in-person meetings and events scheduled for Thursday, including Clematis by Night. The city also canceled in-person meetings and events scheduled to begin or continue after 5 p.m. The city's local state of emergency is extended through Nov. 22 as the city continues recovery from earlier flooding and prepares for more rain. Schools: Palm Beach County public schools are open Thursday, but will be closed on Friday, according to the district. Only West Boca High is closed Thursday because of flooding in the parking lot. Martin County MARTY transit: The county’s current notice says ADA paratransit service has been restored and fixed-route service has resumed on the U.S. Riders can call 772-463-2860 for updates. Schools: Martin County schools and after-school activities are scheduled to resume Thursday after activities were canceled Wednesday. The county’s online Cone Zone map lists roads closed because of flooding. Check it before traveling. Lucie County County parks: Weldon B. Lewis Park, White City Park, Ocean Bay Beach Park and Walton Rocks Beach are listed as closed until further notice because of flooding. Some preserve trails are also flooded. Fort Pierce: City parks, recreation facilities and beach access points have been closed since Tuesday afternoon, Nov. The closures include the River Walk Center and Fort Pierce Recreation Center. Lucie County Public Schools will be closed on Friday, citing an "abundance of caution" due to the projected forecast. All after-school activities are also cancelled. RELATED: Rain floods Port St. Here’s where police spotted high water Roads: The county’s flood update lists a closure at 6547 N. 1 near Cypress Bay Mobile Home Park. Southwest Ann Arbor Road’s 2700 block is no longer flooded but remains closed because of a large pothole. Lucie County schools were closed Wednesday, Nov. 18, and reopened Thursday. Indian River County Schools and district offices: Closed Thursday and Friday because of weather impacts. County government offices, courthouses and Indian River State College campuses are listed as open. Schools will also be closed for Thanksgiving break from Nov. They are scheduled to reopen Monday, Nov. Waste services: The Roseland Customer Convenience Center is closed today because flooding on 130th Street makes it unsafe to reach. The landfill, Gifford and Winter Beach centers are open; curbside collection is running, though routes may be affected by flooded streets. RELATED: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close P arks and facilities : Ambersands Beach Access and Turtle Trail Beach Access are closed. Middleton’s Fish Camp is closed because of flooding. The North County and Gifford aquatic centers, and the public shooting range, are closed Thursday because of site conditions. Other access : Wabasso Beach Park’s beach access has reopened by the ramp, but its stairs remain closed. At Round Island Riverside Beach Park, the mangrove boardwalk and T-Dock are closed; the park itself is listed as open. Okeechobee County Okeechobee County’s local state of emergency was extended through Nov. The state’s flood recovery page also lists recovery resource centers in Okeechobee, Martin and Palm Beach counties; Brevard centers are temporarily closed because of weather Broward County Broward County: All county libraries are closed Thursday because of flooding. The county’s closures page also lists county offices and parks as closed; check Broward County’s site for the latest operational status. Schools: Broward County Public Schools were closed Thursday and will be closed again on Friday. Miami-Dade Clerk of the Court: The clerk’s offices are closed Thursday because of weather. Other closures and notices Palm Beach Zoo: A closure notice supplied to CBS12 says the zoo is closed Thursday because flooding left pathways and exhibits inaccessible. It says the animals and staff are safe. Boca Raton The South Beach Pavilion and part of the surrounding beach area are closed while the city assesses damage from a vehicle accident. This is a separate, non-weather closure. For road conditions, closures and service changes, check local government and agency alerts before leaving. A flood watch remains in effect for parts of South Florida, and conditions can change quickly.

entry.title: West Palm Beach and Vero Beach set new rainfall records after heavy South Florida rain - WPBF
entry.summary: West Palm Beach and Vero Beach set new rainfall records after heavy South Florida rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Heavy rain that moved across South Florida on Thursday helped break daily rainfall records in both West Palm Beach and Vero Beach. Both cities recorded more rain on Nov. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 West Palm Beach received 3.08 inches of rain, breaking the previous record of 2.99 inches set in 2021. Vero Beach recorded 2.25 inches of rainfall, topping the previous record of 1.73 inches set in 1987. The record-setting totals came after rounds of rain moved through parts of South Florida and the Treasure Coast. While the wet weather has eased, residents could still see a few lingering showers heading into the weekend. For Friday, temperatures are expected to remain near normal for this time of year, with highs in the upper 70s and low 80s. Conditions will be cloudy, and some areas could wake up to fog during the morning hours. A stray shower cannot be ruled out, although rain chances remain low. On Saturday, a mix of sun and clouds is expected with highs in the low 80s. Isolated afternoon showers will be possible, with rain chances around 30%. Looking ahead, drier weather is forecast beginning Sunday. Most of next week is expected to stay dry, though a cold front approaching Wednesday could bring a few showers. The front is also expected to cool temperatures into the mid-70s by Thanksgiving. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more rain possible - Sebastian Daily
entry.summary: Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more rain possible    Sebastian Daily
entry.article_text: Home Business News and Economic Updates in Sebastian, Florida Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more rain possible by Andy Hodges Nov 19, 2026 / 5:51 PM A A A A Reset Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch Share on Twitter Share via Email INDIAN RIVER COUNTY — Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch, with a continued risk of excessive rainfall through Saturday, the National Weather Service said Thursday. There is a medium chance — 40% to 60% — of 3 to 6 inches of additional rainfall along the east-central Florida coast through Saturday, according to the National Weather Service office in Melbourne. Because the soil is already saturated from recent heavy rain, many areas are more prone to flooding. Officials said precise locations of the heaviest rainfall remain uncertain. If the most likely rainfall totals materialize, scattered pockets of flooding may develop along the coast, the forecast said. There is a 10% chance of higher-end totals of 8 to 10 inches or more in some locations. Those amounts would bring a risk of impactful flash flooding. The Indian River County Emergency Operations Center continues to monitor weather and road conditions. Officials urged residents to stay home if they do not need to travel. Floodwater and road damage can be difficult to see after dark, the EOC said. Residents should check the county’s road closure map before traveling and never drive through flooded roadways or around barricades. A road may be unsafe even if it is not shown as closed on the map. Multiple roads in the Vero Lake Estates area and elsewhere in the county have already seen closures or standing water this week because of the saturated ground. Minor flooding is already occurring. Up to 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. - Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Sebastian, Fellsmere, Indian River Shores, Sebastian Highlands, Wabasso, Winter Beach, Vero Lake Estates, Sebastian Inlet State Park, Orchid, North Beach, Wabasso Beach and Disneys Vero Beach Resort.
